claims.text: A controlled post-solidification aging treatment will form coherent nanoscale precipitates in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The aging-induced nanoprecipitates will be uniformly distributed.
The precipitates will form within the matrix and along grain boundaries.
Aging at a sufficiently high temperature will activate precipitate nucleation.
Keeping the aging temperature and duration below an over-aging regime will prevent significant precipitate coarsening.
The coherent nanoprecipitates will impede crack initiation.
The coherent nanoprecipitates will impede crack propagation.
The coherent nanoprecipitates will facilitate strain accommodation.
The proposed aging treatment will increase tensile strain-to-failure relative to the untreated alloy.
The proposed aging treatment will increase uniform deformability relative to the untreated alloy.
The precipitate-mediated ductility improvement will not substantially undermine dislocation-based strengthening.
The aged alloy will maintain high yield strength relative to the untreated baseline.
The aged alloy will retain impact-induced energy-release performance comparable to that of the untreated baseline.
Over-aging and precipitate coarsening may deteriorate the alloy's mechanical properties.
The balance among ductility, strength, and energy release may be sensitive to small changes in aging temperature and duration.

contradictions.description: The target property is impact-induced energy release, but the proposed decisive measurement is impact energy absorption. These are not interchangeable and can represent different or opposing energy dispositions, so the experiment does not directly test the stated energy-release claim.
Uniform deformability is a stated outcome, but the listed tensile measurements include strain-to-failure rather than a direct measure such as uniform elongation or strain-field uniformity.
